fixes.explanation: Luke 4:15 says He taught in their synagogues and “…was glorified by everyone.” Everyone, friend. The news about Him had spread throughout the surrounding region too. I can't even get a whole family to agree on one cookie shape, so that's a big deal.

The verse says nothing about anyone walking out. It says He taught in their synagogues and was glorified by everyone. I've watched people leave a kitchen when the dough ran out, but this is nothing like that. The people here are praising Him.
Luke 4:16 says it plainly: “Then Jesus came to Nazareth, where He had been brought up.” This is His hometown. Keep that in mind for what comes next.
Bethany was the village of Mary and Martha (John 11:1), so it's a real place in Jesus' story. It's just not the one in this passage. Luke 4:16 names Nazareth as the town where He was brought up.

The reading says He has sent Me to proclaim “…recovery of sight to the blind…” That's right there in Luke 4:18. So the poor are to hear good news, and the blind are to hear a proclamation of recovery of sight. That list is longer than my cookie order on a holiday.

The rich aren't on the list in the reading. In Luke 4:18 the speaker is sent to preach good news to the poor, to proclaim liberty to the captives, to proclaim recovery of sight to the blind, and to release the oppressed. The blind are the ones named on this card.
The text says the opposite. Luke 4:20 says, “The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on Him…” Nobody is looking away or going back to their own business. Every eye in that room is on Him.
Luke 4:20 says, “The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on Him…” Everyone is watching, not wandering off. I think a room with every eye on Him is waiting to hear what He says next.

The crowd asks, “Isn’t this the son of Joseph?” (Luke 4:22) They ask whose son He is, and Joseph is the name they give. I think they're trying to figure out how the local guy got so impressive. People do that at family reunions all the time.

Jesus says they'll tell Him, “Do here in Your hometown what we have heard that You did in Capernaum.” (Luke 4:23) Capernaum is the town Jesus names there. In that saying, the ask is to do those same things in His hometown.
Jericho isn't mentioned in this passage. In Luke 4:23 Jesus says they'll tell Him to do in His hometown what they have heard that He did in Capernaum. That's the town Jesus names.
Hebron doesn't show up in this passage. The town Jesus names in Luke 4:23 is Capernaum. He says they'll tell Him to do in His hometown what they have heard He did there.
Jesus says the opposite. In Luke 4:24 He says, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his hometown.” A prophet is not accepted there, so honored most doesn't fit.

Jesus says the opposite about Elijah, the prophet. Luke 4:26 reads, “Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to the widow of Zarephath in Sidon.” There were many widows in Israel, but Elijah was sent to none of them. That one can trip you up.

Jesus is talking about Elijah, the prophet. He says, “Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to the widow of Zarephath in Sidon.” (Luke 4:26) Many widows in Israel, and Elijah wasn't sent to any of them. He was sent somewhere else.
Nineveh isn't named in this passage. Luke 4:26 says Elijah was sent to the widow of Zarephath in Sidon. Look for the widow's town in that verse, friend.
Tarsus in Cilicia isn't named in this passage. Luke 4:26 says Elijah was sent to the widow of Zarephath in Sidon. That's the town to hold onto.

Jesus says there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, “Yet not one of them was cleansed—only Naaman the Syrian.” (Luke 4:27) Naaman is the one Jesus names. Not one of those lepers in Israel was cleansed, and He names a Syrian instead.
Hazael isn't named in this passage. In Luke 4:27 the one Jesus names as cleansed is Naaman the Syrian. Jesus says not one of the lepers in Israel was cleansed, only him.
Luke 4:28 says, “On hearing this, all the people in the synagogue were enraged.” All of them. It's a heavy turn. Earlier in the passage, they were speaking well of Him (Luke 4:22).
